transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah… I’m here because I keep getting up when I’m not supposed to. Like at work, I’m supposed to stay at my station, and I’ll just suddenly walk off or pop up like I need to go do something, and sometimes I don’t even really think it through first. It’s like my body moves before my brain catches up.

And it’s not just work — in meetings too, when I’m supposed to stay seated and listen, I’ll stand up or start moving around, and people notice. My supervisor has talked to me about it more than once, and now she’s saying it’s becoming a safety issue, because on the production floor I can’t just leave my spot or take off randomly. I don’t mean to cause problems, but I keep doing it, and it’s starting to get serious.
Do you feel restless or like you need to move when this happens?

Yeah, definitely. It’s not just like I’m bored or I’m choosing to wander off. It feels like this pressure starts building up in my body, especially if I’m standing still by the machine or sitting through training. Like my legs want to go before I’ve even decided anything.

I’ll be trying to stay where I’m supposed to be, and I can feel myself getting more and more uncomfortable, like I need to move right then — pace, stretch, walk away, go check something, anything. If I don’t move, it feels almost unbearable, like I’m trapped in place. Then I’ll just get up or start shifting around before I even fully think about it.
Do you feel anxious or upset when this pressure to move builds up inside you?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it anxiety exactly, but I do get really uncomfortable and kind of worked up when it builds. Like if I’m trying to stand still by the machine, or if I’m sitting through training and I’m supposed to just stay there and pay attention, it feels like this pressure is rising in my body.

It’s like I have to move right then — pace, stretch, shift around, go do something, anything. And if I try to force myself not to, I start feeling more and more bothered, like I’m trapped in my own skin almost. So yeah, I get upset in the sense that it feels unbearable, and then I just end up moving before I can really talk myself out of it.
Did you experience these feelings of restlessness and needing to move when you were a child?

Yeah, I did. I mean, looking back, that was kind of always me, even when I was little. In elementary school I was the kid who could not stay in my seat. Like, the teacher would tell everyone to sit down and do their work, and I’d be up sharpening a pencil, walking around, messing with something, or just kind of drifting away from my desk without really thinking about it.

And I talked over the teacher a lot too. Not always trying to be rude, but I’d just blurt things out, answer before I was called on, interrupt because the thought was there and it felt like I had to say it right then. I remember getting notes sent home for that — for talking too much, blurting out, getting out of my seat, wandering around the classroom. It was pretty much a thing people noticed about me even back then.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted or having trouble focusing on tasks?

Yeah, very easily. At work especially, on the line, it doesn’t take much at all. Like I can be at my station knowing I’m supposed to keep my eyes on what I’m doing, and then one beep from a different machine will happen, or somebody walks by with a pallet jack, and it’s like my eyes go there before I even choose to look.

And it’s not just my eyes, it’s like my whole brain gets pulled over there with it. I’ll be thinking about that sound or watching where they’re going, and then I have to drag myself back to my own station like, “No, focus on this.” But it happens over and over, even when I know I need to stay locked in. It’s frustrating because I’m not trying to ignore my task — it’s just really easy for something else to grab me.
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they finish speaking?

Yeah… I do that a lot, honestly. I don’t usually mean it like I’m trying to be rude, but I’ll cut in before I even realize I’m doing it.

Like at work, if a couple coworkers are talking about something and I hear part of it, I’ll just jump in with my thought, even if nobody was really talking to me. Or if the lead is explaining something or asking a question, I’ll answer before they’re even done finishing the sentence, because I think I already know where they’re going with it. Then sometimes I’m wrong, or I’ve talked over them, and everybody kind of looks irritated.

It’s embarrassing because afterward I can tell I did it again, but in the moment it feels like the words just come out before I’ve had time to stop them. I’ve had people be like, “Let me finish,” or “I wasn’t asking you,” and then I feel bad, but it still keeps happening.
Have your symptoms caused problems in your personal relationships?

Yeah, it has. I mean, it affects people around me, but the biggest place it’s been really obvious is at work, because that kind of spills into relationships with coworkers too.

Like, I’ve been written up by supervisors for safety stuff and production problems, and it’s not just a little warning where everyone forgets about it. It feels like it follows me. I’m trying to keep my job, and I’ve been wanting to work toward getting certified, but when I keep getting written up or people see me as someone who causes problems on the line, it makes that feel like it could get taken away from me.

And with coworkers, it’s gotten awkward. During handoffs, people don’t always want to partner with me or depend on me because they’re worried something will get missed or messed up. I can tell they get frustrated, and then I feel embarrassed and kind of on edge, because I know they’re thinking, like, “Great, I have to work with her again.” So yeah, it’s not just inside my head — it’s actually affecting how people deal with me and whether they trust me at work.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking, like grabbing something or doing something physical without considering the consequences?

Yeah… that’s actually one of the main reasons I came in. I keep doing this thing where I just leave my station before I’ve really thought it through. Like I’m supposed to stay put on the line, and something will happen or I’ll feel like I need to check something, and I’m already walking away before I’ve even stopped to think, “Am I allowed to leave right now?” or “Is this safe?”

It happens in meetings too. If we’re supposed to be sitting there listening, I’ll pop up or move around like I’m going to go do something, and then I realize people are looking at me because I wasn’t supposed to get up. It’s not like I plan it out. It’s more like my body starts moving first, and then my brain catches up after.

My supervisor has been on me about it because on the floor it can become a safety issue. Like if I step away from my station at the wrong time or just take off without letting someone know, it can mess with the process or put me where I shouldn’t be. And I hate that, because I’m not trying to be careless, but I do act before I think a lot. That “just go” feeling happens really fast.
Are your symptoms causing problems in your relationships with family or friends?

I’m honestly not totally sure how much it’s affected family or friends, like not in a big obvious way that I can point to the same way I can with work. I mean, I’m sure I probably annoy people sometimes or talk too fast or jump into things, but nobody in my family has sat me down like, “This is ruining our relationship,” or anything like that.

With friends, I don’t know… I don’t have a clear example where I can say, yes, this caused a fight or ended a friendship. Sometimes I worry I’m a lot to deal with, but that might just be me overthinking it. So I guess I’d say I haven’t really noticed major problems there, or at least not ones people have directly told me about.
Have you experienced these symptoms of restlessness and impulsivity consistently over the years, or have they varied in intensity?

It’s been more like… it’s gotten seriously noticeable over the last year and a little bit. I’d say about a year and two months, give or take. That’s when it really started causing problems, not just being something I could brush off.

It kind of lined up with when I was trying to tighten up my habits at work and actually move forward, like working toward forklift and CNC certification. I was trying to be more serious and prove I could handle more responsibility, and that’s when these things started standing out more because I couldn’t just wing it anymore. Like before, maybe I was restless or impulsive and just thought, “That’s how I am,” but once I was trying to be consistent and follow everything exactly, it became a real issue.

So I don’t know if it was there before and I just didn’t pay as much attention, but the serious problems from it have been going on for about a year and two months.
Have you experienced these symptoms consistently since childhood?

Yeah, I mean… thinking back, yes. It wasn’t just something that started as an adult. Even in elementary school I was kind of known as the kid who couldn’t just sit still and stay in my seat like everybody else.

I remember getting in trouble for talking over the teacher, like blurting stuff out before I was supposed to, or answering when it wasn’t my turn. And I’d get notes sent home because I’d be wandering around the classroom or getting up when I wasn’t supposed to. It wasn’t like I was trying to be bad, at least not how I remember it. I just felt like I had to move or say the thing right then, and then afterward I’d realize I was in trouble again.

So yeah, it’s been there since I was little. It just looks more serious now because the consequences are bigger.
Have you experienced significant problems due to these symptoms in multiple settings, such as at work, at home, or in social situations, as an adult?

As an adult, the biggest place it’s caused real problems is work. That’s where it’s not just embarrassing or annoying, it’s actually putting things at risk for me.

I’ve been written up by supervisors for safety stuff and production issues, and that’s really scary because I’m trying to move forward, not mess up the job I already have. I’ve been trying to get to a point where I can do more, like with the forklift and CNC certification plans, and when I get written up it feels like I’m proving the opposite, like I can’t be trusted with more responsibility.

And it’s not only the supervisors. Coworkers notice too. During handoffs, people seem less willing to partner with me or rely on me, and I can tell there’s this hesitation, like they’re thinking, “Is this going to be a problem?” That part bothers me a lot because I don’t want to be seen as unsafe or difficult to work with.

At home or socially, I don’t have as clear of examples, but at work, yes, definitely. It’s been significant there.
Have you felt like your symptoms have significantly impacted your ability to function or caused a lot of distress in your daily life?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, the biggest thing is work, because that’s where it feels like it’s actually affecting my life in a real way, not just making me feel uncomfortable or frustrated.

It’s put my job at risk, honestly. I’ve had supervisors write me up for safety and production problems, and every time that happens I get this awful feeling like, “Okay, this is going on my record, this could mess everything up.” I’m trying to move forward there, not just stay stuck, and I’ve been wanting to work toward certifications like forklift and CNC, but when I’m getting written up it makes it seem like I’m not reliable enough for that. Like why would they trust me with more responsibility if I’m already having problems now?

And it’s stressful with coworkers too. During handoffs, I can tell some people are less willing to partner with me or depend on me. It’s not always something they say directly, but you can feel it when someone hesitates or double-checks everything because they don’t really trust you. That really bothers me, because I don’t want to be seen as unsafe or like I’m making everyone else’s job harder.

So yes, it’s caused a lot of distress. I think about it even after I leave work, because it feels like this could affect my whole future there.
Have you experienced these symptoms of restlessness and impulsivity in a consistent pattern since childhood, without any significant periods where they completely went away?

Yes, it’s been pretty consistent. I don’t really remember a time where it just fully went away and I was suddenly calm or able to sit still like everyone else.

Even in elementary school, I was that kid who couldn’t stay in my seat. Like, I’d get up or kind of wander around the room when I wasn’t supposed to, and teachers would send notes home about it. I also talked over the teacher a lot, or I’d blurt things out before it was my turn. It wasn’t like I had some big plan to be disruptive — it was more like the words or the need to move would happen before I really stopped to think.

So yeah, from when I was little, that pattern was there. It’s not something I can point to and say, “Oh, that disappeared for a few years.” It’s just kind of always been part of how I was.
Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty sustaining focus during tasks, in the past 6 months?

Yes, I have. It’s been happening a lot, especially with things at work that I’m supposed to sit with and actually process.

Like when I’m doing inventory logs, I’ll start off really trying to pay attention. I’ll tell myself, “Okay, just slow down, read the numbers, make sure you’re entering it right.” But after a few minutes, it’s like the numbers start running together. I’ll realize I’ve been looking at the page or the screen but I didn’t actually take it in, so then I have to go back and check the same line again.

It happens with the CNC training pages too. I want to understand them because that’s something I’m trying to work toward, so it’s not like I don’t care. But I’ll read a paragraph and then get to the end and think, “Wait, what did that even say?” Then I go back, and sometimes I have to reread the same part a few times because the words just kind of blur together after a little while.

It’s frustrating because I’ll be trying, but my focus just doesn’t hold very long.
Have your symptoms of restlessness, impulsivity, and inattention continued into your adult life without any significant remission?

Yeah, it has continued into adulthood. I wouldn’t say there was some clear break where it all stopped and then came back.

The part where it started causing really serious problems, though, has been about a year and two months now. That’s when I really tried to tighten up my habits at work and take things more seriously, because I wanted to move toward getting forklift and CNC certified. I was trying to be more consistent and prove I could handle more responsibility, and that’s when it became really obvious that this wasn’t just me being young or needing to try harder.

Like, the more I tried to push myself into that “reliable adult at work” role, the more these issues started getting in the way in a serious way. So yes, it’s been there into adult life, but the major problems from it have been especially noticeable for about the last year and two months.
Have you experienced any problems in your personal or social relationships due to your symptoms?

Yeah, mostly at work, honestly. I don’t know if that counts as social relationships exactly, but it affects how people deal with me there, like coworkers and supervisors.

I’ve been written up by supervisors for safety stuff and production problems, and that’s been really stressful because it makes me feel like my job is kind of on the line. And it’s also made the certification stuff I’m trying to work toward feel less possible, because if they already see me as someone who causes problems or needs correcting, then I worry they’re not going to trust me with forklift or CNC training.

With coworkers, I can tell some of them are less willing to partner with me during handoffs. Like, they don’t always say it directly, but you can feel it when someone’s kind of annoyed or hesitant to work with you because they think you’re going to make things harder or mess up the flow. That part bothers me a lot, because I don’t want to be seen as unreliable or like someone people have to avoid. It’s embarrassing, and it makes me feel like I’m always trying to catch up and prove I’m not a problem.
Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity-impulsivity for at least 6 months?

Yes. The serious problems from it have been going on for about a year and two months now.

I mean, I’ve had issues before that, but that’s when it really started standing out and affecting things in a bigger way. It was around the time I was trying to tighten up my habits at work and be more responsible, because I wanted to move toward getting forklift and CNC certified. I was really trying to prove I could handle more, but instead it felt like the more I tried to get it together, the more obvious the problems became.

So yes, definitely more than 6 months. It’s been a little over a year, and it’s been serious enough that I can’t really brush it off anymore.
Have you experienced these symptoms at home or in other settings outside of work?

I’m honestly not totally sure how to answer that. Most of what I notice, or at least most of what has caused actual consequences, is at work, because that’s where there are rules and supervisors and people watching whether I mess up.

At home, I mean… I don’t know. I probably have habits that other people would notice more than I do, but I haven’t really been tracking it the same way. It’s not like someone is writing me up at home, so it’s harder for me to say, “Yes, this is the same exact problem happening there.” I just don’t want to overstate it if I’m not sure.

Outside of work, I guess I’d have to think more about what you mean specifically. Like if you mean whether people have complained about me or if I’ve had real problems because of it, I can’t really point to something clear the way I can with work. Work is just where it’s been the most obvious and where it’s actually been affecting my life in a serious way.
Have you experienced these symptoms in settings other than work, such as at home or in social situations?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I know you’re asking outside of work, like home or social stuff, but I don’t have a clear example where I can say, “Yes, this exact thing happened there too.”

At home, there isn’t really the same kind of structure or consequences, so it’s harder for me to tell. Like, nobody’s standing there keeping track or writing me up, so I don’t know if I’m just not noticing it or if it’s not as much of a problem there. And with social situations, I can’t think of anything specific right now where someone has directly said it’s an issue.

I don’t want to say no, because maybe there are things I’m missing, but I also don’t want to make it sound like I have proof of it happening everywhere. Work is just the place where it’s been the most obvious and where it has caused real problems.

target_item.reason: The question asks about physically acting on impulse without thinking about consequences, which is best matched by leaving the station or popping up when expected to stay put, described as taking off before thinking and causing safety problems.

patient.answer:
Yeah… that’s actually one of the main reasons I came in. I keep doing this thing where I just leave my station before I’ve really thought it through. Like I’m supposed to stay put on the line, and something will happen or I’ll feel like I need to check something, and I’m already walking away before I’ve even stopped to think, “Am I allowed to leave right now?” or “Is this safe?”

It happens in meetings too. If we’re supposed to be sitting there listening, I’ll pop up or move around like I’m going to go do something, and then I realize people are looking at me because I wasn’t supposed to get up. It’s not like I plan it out. It’s more like my body starts moving first, and then my brain catches up after.

My supervisor has been on me about it because on the floor it can become a safety issue. Like if I step away from my station at the wrong time or just take off without letting someone know, it can mess with the process or put me where I shouldn’t be. And I hate that, because I’m not trying to be careless, but I do act before I think a lot. That “just go” feeling happens really fast.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are significantly impacting their daily life and relationships outside of work

I mean, I’m sure I probably annoy people sometimes or talk too fast or jump into things, but nobody in my family has sat me down like, “This is ruining our relationship,” or anything like that.

With friends, I don’t know… I don’t have a clear example where I can say, yes, this caused a fight or ended a friendship. Sometimes I worry I’m a lot to deal with, but that might just be me overthinking it. So I guess I’d say I haven’t really noticed major problems there, or at least not ones people have directly told me about.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms have persisted consistently over time
doctor.question: Have you experienced these symptoms of restlessness and impulsivity consistently over the years, or have they varied in intensity?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been causing serious problems for about 1 year and 2 months, ever since I tried to tighten up my habits and move toward forklift and CNC certification.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how long the restlessness and impulsivity have been present and whether their intensity has changed over time.

patient.answer:
It’s been more like… it’s gotten seriously noticeable over the last year and a little bit. I’d say about a year and two months, give or take. That’s when it really started causing problems, not just being something I could brush off.

It kind of lined up with when I was trying to tighten up my habits at work and actually move forward, like working toward forklift and CNC certification. I was trying to be more serious and prove I could handle more responsibility, and that’s when these things started standing out more because I couldn’t just wing it anymore. Like before, maybe I was restless or impulsive and just thought, “That’s how I am,” but once I was trying to be consistent and follow everything exactly, it became a real issue.

So I don’t know if it was there before and I just didn’t pay as much attention, but the serious problems from it have been going on for about a year and two months.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the criteria for persistence over time
doctor.question: Have you experienced these symptoms consistently since childhood?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Even in elementary school, I was the kid who couldn't stay in my seat, talked over the teacher, and got notes sent home for blurting things out or wandering around the room.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms have been present consistently since childhood, which directly relates to onset before age 12.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I mean… thinking back, yes. It wasn’t just something that started as an adult. Even in elementary school I was kind of known as the kid who couldn’t just sit still and stay in my seat like everybody else.

I remember getting in trouble for talking over the teacher, like blurting stuff out before I was supposed to, or answering when it wasn’t my turn. And I’d get notes sent home because I’d be wandering around the classroom or getting up when I wasn’t supposed to. It wasn’t like I was trying to be bad, at least not how I remember it. I just felt like I had to move or say the thing right then, and then afterward I’d realize I was in trouble again.

So yeah, it’s been there since I was little. It just looks more serious now because the consequences are bigger.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the criteria for persistence into adulthood
doctor.question: Have you experienced significant problems due to these symptoms in multiple settings, such as at work, at home, or in social situations, as an adult?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: At work this has put my job and certification plans at risk, because supervisors have written me up for safety and production problems and coworkers are less willing to partner with me during handoffs.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is asking whether the symptoms cause significant impairment in adult life across settings; this directly matches the functional impairment criterion.

patient.answer:
As an adult, the biggest place it’s caused real problems is work. That’s where it’s not just embarrassing or annoying, it’s actually putting things at risk for me.

I’ve been written up by supervisors for safety stuff and production issues, and that’s really scary because I’m trying to move forward, not mess up the job I already have. I’ve been trying to get to a point where I can do more, like with the forklift and CNC certification plans, and when I get written up it feels like I’m proving the opposite, like I can’t be trusted with more responsibility.

And it’s not only the supervisors. Coworkers notice too. During handoffs, people seem less willing to partner with me or rely on me, and I can tell there’s this hesitation, like they’re thinking, “Is this going to be a problem?” That part bothers me a lot because I don’t want to be seen as unsafe or difficult to work with.

At home or socially, I don’t have as clear of examples, but at work, yes, definitely. It’s been significant there.

doctor.intent: Determine if the symptoms have caused significant distress or impairment in social or occupational functioning

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: At work this has put my job and certification plans at risk, because supervisors have written me up for safety and production problems and coworkers are less willing to partner with me during handoffs.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms have significantly affected functioning or caused distress in daily life, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah, definitely. I mean, the biggest thing is work, because that’s where it feels like it’s actually affecting my life in a real way, not just making me feel uncomfortable or frustrated.

It’s put my job at risk, honestly. I’ve had supervisors write me up for safety and production problems, and every time that happens I get this awful feeling like, “Okay, this is going on my record, this could mess everything up.” I’m trying to move forward there, not just stay stuck, and I’ve been wanting to work toward certifications like forklift and CNC, but when I’m getting written up it makes it seem like I’m not reliable enough for that. Like why would they trust me with more responsibility if I’m already having problems now?

And it’s stressful with coworkers too. During handoffs, I can tell some people are less willing to partner with me or depend on me. It’s not always something they say directly, but you can feel it when someone hesitates or double-checks everything because they don’t really trust you. That really bothers me, because I don’t want to be seen as unsafe or like I’m making everyone else’s job harder.

So yes, it’s caused a lot of distress. I think about it even after I leave work, because it feels like this could affect my whole future there.

doctor.intent: determine if the symptoms meet the criteria for persistence across the lifespan

Yes, it’s been pretty consistent. I don’t really remember a time where it just fully went away and I was suddenly calm or able to sit still like everyone else.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the persistence criterion for ADHD
doctor.question: Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty sustaining focus during tasks, in the past 6 months?

target_item.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: When I'm doing inventory logs or reading the CNC training pages, I start out really trying, but after a few minutes the numbers or words blur together and I have to keep going back because I didn't take any of it in.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about inattention and difficulty sustaining focus during tasks, which directly matches this symptom.

patient.answer:
Yes, I have. It’s been happening a lot, especially with things at work that I’m supposed to sit with and actually process.

Like when I’m doing inventory logs, I’ll start off really trying to pay attention. I’ll tell myself, “Okay, just slow down, read the numbers, make sure you’re entering it right.” But after a few minutes, it’s like the numbers start running together. I’ll realize I’ve been looking at the page or the screen but I didn’t actually take it in, so then I have to go back and check the same line again.

It happens with the CNC training pages too. I want to understand them because that’s something I’m trying to work toward, so it’s not like I don’t care. But I’ll read a paragraph and then get to the end and think, “Wait, what did that even say?” Then I go back, and sometimes I have to reread the same part a few times because the words just kind of blur together after a little while.

It’s frustrating because I’ll be trying, but my focus just doesn’t hold very long.
